KEY MESSAGE 1...Unsettled weather continues today, before giving way 
to a brief period of mainly dry conditions tonight through most of 
Sunday.

A deep...vertically stacked low over Maine will continue to make its 
way east across the Canadian Maritimes today...with one more 
shortwave disturbance and attendant plume of somewhat deeper 
moisture on its backside sliding across our area from west to east 
during the course of the day. This latter feature will help to 
generate another brief round of scattered to numerous showers as it 
crosses our area...while also helping to temporarily reinvigorate 
some ongoing nuisance lake effect/upslope rain showers east of the 
lakes. Throughout today thermal profiles will remain warm enough for 
rain to again predominate...with 850 mb temps of -2C/-3C only 
allowing for a few wet snowflakes to mix in across the higher 
terrain of the Southern Tier and Tug Hill early this morning. 

Following the passage of the aforementioned shortwave and plume of 
deeper moisture...corresponding subsidence and drying out of the 
column will allow our area to dry out from west to east this 
afternoon and early this evening. Meanwhile...a tightening pressure 
gradient will lead to a short round of breezy to windy conditions 
for WNY featuring gusts to 25-30 mph in most locations...and locally 
up to 35 mph downwind of Lake Erie. 

As we make our way through tonight...a marginally favorable 
environment (850 mb temps of -1C to -2C) for lake effect pcpn will 
linger across our region. While our airmass will be relatively dry 
initially...another brief/subtle increase in background moisture may 
be enough to support the redevelopment of a few more spotty lake 
effect rain showers east/east-northeast of both lakes...with a few 
wet snowflakes again possible across the higher terrain of the Tug 
Hill and western Adirondack foothills. Increasing drying and 
subsidence associated with the approach/passage of a narrow low- 
level ridge will then help to squelch any such showers from west to 
east later tonight and Sunday morning...while otherwise providing 
our region with an interlude of dry weather through early to mid 
Sunday afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Another round of widespread showers will cross the 
region Sunday night and early Monday, with a few leftover rain and 
snow showers then following through Tuesday morning.

By later Sunday afternoon the low-level ridge will be sliding east 
across New England...while the next mid-level trough and associated 
surface low makes its way across the Mississippi and Lower Ohio 
Valleys. Deepening moisture and attendant height falls/DCVA aloft 
out ahead of this system may allow for a few showers to make it into 
far WNY late Sunday afternoon...with more widespread rain showers 
then crossing the region from west to east Sunday night and early 
Monday as the axis of the increasingly negatively-tilted trough and 
deepening surface low pivot northeastward across our region. While 
rainfall amounts from this system will be somewhat held in check by 
its rapid movement...the impressive forcing and deep moisture should 
still be supportive of a general quarter to half inch of additional 
rainfall. 

Following the passage of this system...a west-northwesterly flow of 
colder air will overspread our region Monday and Monday night... 
sending 850 mb temps down to between -6C and -9C. While this 
incoming airmass will be plenty cold enough to provoke a lake 
response...deeper synoptic-scale moisture will quickly get stripped 
away during the course of Monday...with this and the relatively 
short fetch helping to keep this response rather limited. Thus... 
while there should be at least a few rain and snow showers east-
southeast of the lakes Monday afternoon through Tuesday morning... 
these should remain limited in scope and capable of only some spotty 
light snow accumulations. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...A round of gusty downslope winds is possible along 
the Lake Erie shoreline Sunday evening, followed by more widespread 
windy conditions on Monday.

Out ahead of the Sunday night system...an increasing south-
southeasterly flow in the lowest couple thousand feel AGL may bring 
a brief round of gusty downslope winds to areas downwind of the 
Chautauqua ridge during Sunday evening. While inconsistencies 
amongst the shorter-term guidance in the strength of the low level 
wind field and potential low-level stabilization from the system's 
rain showers lead to lower confidence in the strength and duration 
of any such winds...it at least appears that some gusts to 30-35 mph 
will be possible for a time in favored areas along the Lake Erie 
shoreline.
